newsitem.title: SWEDEN: ASBRINK SAYS SWEDISH BANKS "MODEST" IN BALTICS.
newsitem.headline: ASBRINK SAYS SWEDISH BANKS "MODEST" IN BALTICS.

text.p: Swedish Finance Minister Erik Asbrink on Wednesday urged his country's banks to get more involved in the development of the Baltic states and said they had played only a "very modest role" so far.
Despite strong historical trading links, only one Swedish bank, Handelsbanken , has made a move in the post-Soviet Baltics by buying small Estonian broker Aktoris.

"Swedish banks have played a very modest role in the Baltic financial sector. It would be in their interests to participate in neighbouring countries," Asbrink told a Euromoney conference on investing in the Baltic capital markets.
But he conceded that the hesitancy of Swedish financial institutions to get involved in the Baltics was natural due to the volatile nature of each country's financial sector.

Estonia, Lithuania and Latvia have all suffered banking crises. Estonia is now seen as having the most advanced and stable financial sector and its banks have begun expanding out of their small home market into the other two countries.
